# ACR Drift Report — ShiftLine Workforce Scheduling, v9.3 → v9.6

**Prepared for:** City of Marlow, IT Procurement (renewal review)
**Subject product:** ShiftLine Workforce Scheduling (third-party vendor product)
**Prior document:** vendor ACR, product version 9.3, `report_date: 2026-06-12`, received 2026-06-30
**Current document:** vendor ACR, product version 9.6, `report_date: 2027-01-08`, received 2027-01-15
**Catalog (both documents):** `2.5-edition-wcag-2.2-508-en`
**Inputs used:** the two documents above and nothing else. No evaluation of v9.6 was commissioned; no sample was drawn; no testing session was run.

---

## 1. Pair classification: FOREIGN

Both documents were authored by ShiftLine's accessibility office, and — the determining test — **neither document's adherence notes carry a `finding_id` or a `fingerprint`**. Every note in both files is prose only ("Fully supported.", "No prerecorded media in the product.", "A fix is on the roadmap."). Nothing in either document traces to an evidence record the city holds.

That makes this a **foreign pair**, and the classification sets the ceiling on what this report can produce:

| | |
|---|---|
| Available output | **SC-level term deltas only** |
| Not available | Finding-level trend of any kind. The trend vocabulary requires our own prior fingerprints in both documents; there are none, so no trend term is used anywhere in this report and none can be inferred from it. |

Authorship is not what decides this. Our own pre-fingerprint output would classify identically. The city's closed `mar-2026v1` verification engagement against the v9.3 demo tenant is out of scope for this request and is not used here — its findings are v9.3 evidence, not a fingerprint set embedded in either document, and reaching for them would manufacture a comparison history the documents do not contain.

---

## 2. What this report is, and what it is not

This report compares **a claim against an earlier claim**. It reads two documents. It tests nothing, verifies nothing, and commissions nothing.

**A term delta here is not a product delta.** Every row below records that the vendor wrote a different sentence in January 2027 than it wrote in June 2026. No one measured anything between the two documents on the city's behalf. Where the vendor attributes a change to a release (9.4, 9.5) that attribution is the vendor's own statement, carried here as document content, not as a finding.

The only thing that converts a claim change into evidence is commissioning a verification engagement against v9.6 — a WCAG-EM sample of the live product, then a claims-delta report (Lane B). That routing is in the handoff.

---

## 3. Comparability statement (mandatory)

Two ACRs normally rest on two sample sets, and WCAG-EM re-evaluation expects those sets to differ — some samples held in common for comparability, some replaced for coverage. Stating which is which is a required part of any drift report.

**Neither of these documents declares a sample set at all.** Neither carries `evaluation_methods_used`, a sampling statement, a coverage boundary, a tested-configuration list, or a legal disclaimer. There is therefore:

- **no common sample set** between the two cycles that can be named,
- **no replaced or added sample** that can be named,
- **no basis on which any single delta can be attributed to a change in the product** rather than to a change in what the vendor looked at, who looked, or how they wrote it up.

Consequently **every delta row below is marked not comparable**, and the mark is not a defect in one row — it is the condition of the whole pair.

The pair is still diffable, because the two documents agree on the frame:

| Frame element | Prior (9.3) | Current (9.6) | Same? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Product | ShiftLine Workforce Scheduling | ShiftLine Workforce Scheduling | Yes |
| Catalog | `2.5-edition-wcag-2.2-508-en` | `2.5-edition-wcag-2.2-508-en` | Yes |
| Component set | `web` only | `web` only | Yes |
| Conformance target | AAA declared outside target; A/AA populated | identical wording | Yes |
| 508 chapters (FPC, hardware, software, support docs) | all four `disabled: true`, note "Not addressed in this report." | identical | Yes |

Same product, same catalog, same component set, same declared target — so the diff proceeds rather than stopping. But note what the last two rows mean for a 508 procurement: **both cycles cover web only, and neither addresses the four 508 chapters**, including functional performance criteria and support documentation and services. "Not addressed in this report." is a statement of omission, not a coverage boundary. That is unchanged between cycles, so it is not a delta — it is a standing gap in both documents.

One further limit on how much any delta is worth: **44 of 56 rows in the prior document and 46 of 55 in the current one are `supports` with the note "Fully supported."** A note that carries no scope tells the reader nothing about what was examined. That applies to the unchanged rows as much as the changed ones — stability across two documents whose passing notes are contentless is not evidence of a stable product.

---

## 4. SC-level term deltas

Every criterion whose term changed, plus every criterion present in one document and absent from the other. Criteria whose terms are identical appear only in the summary counts in § 6.

| SC | Prior term | Current term | Delta | Comparable? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.2.2 (A) | `not-applicable` | *no row in current document* | Claim withdrawn — the criterion is absent from the current document, with no stated reason | No — no sample set declared in either document | Prior `success_criteria_level_a`, num "1.2.2", note "No prerecorded media in the product." Current `success_criteria_level_a` has no entry for 1.2.2; the list runs 1.2.1 → 1.2.3. |
| 1.4.3 (AA) | `supports` | `partially-supports` | Less favorable claim | No — no sample set declared in either document | Prior note: "All text meets the 4.5:1 minimum." Current note: "Body text on the reporting dashboard does not meet the 4.5:1 minimum; remediation planned for v9.7." |
| 2.4.7 (AA) | `partially-supports` | `supports` | More favorable claim | No — no sample set declared in either document | Prior note: "Known issue: the schedule grid's focus indicator can be difficult to see. A fix is on the roadmap." Current note: "The schedule grid focus indicator was rebuilt in 9.5." |
| 3.1.2 (AA) | `not-evaluated` | `supports` | No-claim → claim asserted. Not movement on the conformance axis; the prior term is not a legal term for a Level AA row in this catalog (see § 5) | No — no sample set declared in either document | Prior note: "Deferred to a future assessment." Current note: "Language of parts is marked throughout." |
| 3.3.3 (AA) | `partially-supports` | `supports` | More favorable claim | No — no sample set declared in either document | Prior note: "Error suggestions are missing on the timeclock form; fix scheduled for v9.4." Current note: "Error suggestions were added to the timeclock form in 9.4." |

Direction is read on the conformance axis `supports = not-applicable > partially-supports > does-not-support`. `not-evaluated` and an absent row are not on that axis, which is why rows 1.2.2 and 3.1.2 carry a description instead of a direction.

---

## 5. Reading the five deltas

**1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) — withdrawn without explanation, and the withdrawal contradicts its neighbor.**
The v9.3 document claimed `not-applicable` on the grounds that the product contains no prerecorded media. The v9.6 document simply has no 1.2.2 row. There is no note explaining the removal.

The obvious benign reading — the product now contains prerecorded media, so the old NA no longer holds — is contradicted inside the current document itself: **1.2.3 still claims `not-applicable` with the note "No prerecorded media in the product."** If that is true, 1.2.2 should still be NA on identical grounds. The current document therefore asserts the absence of prerecorded media on one row while declining to say anything on the neighbouring row that turns on the same fact.

This also makes the current document **incomplete against the catalog it declares**: 55 of 56 A/AA criteria present, where the prior document had all 56. Document completeness moved backwards. A dropped row is not a neutral event in a conformance document — it is the one place where a claim can disappear without anyone having to write "does-not-support."

**1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) — the only claim that moved against the city's interest, and it is self-disclosed.**
The vendor now states that body text on the reporting dashboard fails 4.5:1, with remediation planned for v9.7 — a version that does not exist at renewal and cannot be evaluated.

The pair supports two readings and cannot distinguish between them:

1. The reporting dashboard changed (or arrived) between 9.3 and 9.6 and introduced the failure.
2. The v9.3 claim "All text meets the 4.5:1 minimum" was over-broad when it was made.

Nothing in either document selects between these, because neither declares what was sampled. Reading 2 matters beyond this row: if a blanket "all text" claim was written without a sample that could support it, that bears on the weight of the other 45 `supports` rows in the current document — all of which rest on the same undeclared method.

Note also what did *not* happen: this is a self-disclosed failure the vendor volunteered in a renewal packet. That is more candid than a document that quietly keeps saying `supports`. Candor is not a red flag, and the row is not evidence of vendor bad faith. It is evidence of a documented, unremediated 4.5:1 failure on a named surface.

**2.4.7 Focus Visible and 3.3.3 Error Suggestion — the vendor's account is internally consistent across the two documents.**
In 9.3 the vendor named both defects specifically and committed to fixes: the focus indicator "A fix is on the roadmap," error suggestions "fix scheduled for v9.4." In 9.6 both are claimed `supports` with notes attributing the work to 9.5 and 9.4 respectively — the same releases, in the right order, on the same named surfaces.

That internal consistency raises plausibility. It is not evidence. Two self-reports that agree with each other are still two self-reports, and the city has measured neither. The focus indicator in particular is the kind of claim where "rebuilt" and "sufficient" are different statements: a rebuilt indicator can still fail 2.4.7 or 1.4.11, and nothing in the document distinguishes the work being done from the criterion being met.

**3.1.2 Language of Parts — a claim appearing where there was none, not a defect being cleared.**
The v9.3 document used `not-evaluated` on a Level AA criterion. **The catalog both documents declare restricts `not-evaluated` to WCAG Level AAA criteria.** Used on a Level AA row it is not a conformance position at all — it is a gap in the report wearing a term.

The procurement consequence is precise, and it cuts both ways:

- Do **not** read `not-evaluated → supports` as the vendor fixing something. There was no prior finding, no prior failure, and no prior position to move from.
- Do **not** read the prior `not-evaluated` as an admission of failure either. It said only that the vendor had not looked.

What actually changed is that a criterion the v9.3 document left unanswered now carries a full support claim, backed by a one-sentence note. Of the five deltas, this is the one with the least behind it: the criterion has gone from "we didn't check" to "supports" in a single step, with no method stated in either cycle.

**What none of these rows say.** Two claims moved toward conformance, one moved away, one appeared where there was no claim, one vanished. That is not a product that got better, and it is not a product that got worse. Both documents are self-reported and neither declares a scope, so there is no net direction to compute and none is offered here.

---

## 6. Summary counts

| Measure | Prior (9.3) | Current (9.6) |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog A/AA criteria | 56 (32 A + 24 AA) | 56 (32 A + 24 AA) |
| Criteria with a row | 56 — complete | 55 — 1.2.2 absent |
| `supports` | 44 | 46 |
| `not-applicable` | 9 | 8 |
| `partially-supports` | 2 | 1 |
| `does-not-support` | 0 | 0 |
| `not-evaluated` (illegal at A/AA in this catalog) | 1 | 0 |

**Delta counts**

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Criteria with a row in both documents | 55 |
| Terms identical (reported here and nowhere else) | 51 |
| Terms changed | 4 |
| Row present in exactly one document | 1 |
| **Total delta rows** | **5** |
| Of the changed terms: more favorable claim | 2 (2.4.7, 3.3.3) |
| Of the changed terms: less favorable claim | 1 (1.4.3) |
| Of the changed terms: not on the conformance axis | 1 (3.1.2) |
| Deltas marked comparable | 0 of 5 |

**Scope of these counts:** they describe two vendor documents. They do not describe the ShiftLine product, and no conformance conclusion about v9.6 follows from them.

---

## 7. Trend reporting: not available for this pair

No finding-level trend table appears in this report, and none can be produced from these inputs. Trend is defined against a fingerprint that is verified present or verified absent in a current evaluation; neither document carries fingerprints and no current evaluation exists. Emitting trend language against a foreign pair would fabricate a comparison history the city does not have.

This also means the drift-report gate that normally applies — adjudication of any row claiming a defect has been cleared — has nothing to fire on here, because no such row exists in this report and none legitimately could. Where a defect-cleared row *would* have appeared (2.4.7, 3.3.3), this report gives you a claim change and says so.

---

## 8. Routing

- **Verification of any delta → Lane B (claims verification).** Requires commissioning a WCAG-EM evaluation of v9.6 at a declared scope, then comparing the v9.6 document's claims against the resulting outcome map.
- **Bug filing → not applicable.** Nothing here was verified, so there is nothing filable. Foreign drift never routes to bug reporting; the 1.4.3 disclosure is a vendor statement, not a reproduced defect.
- **No ACR was produced, merged, or corrected by this report**, and neither input document was modified. Producing a city-owned ACR for this product would be a fresh serialization off a fresh evaluation, not an edit of the vendor's file.

---

# Handoff note — City of Marlow, IT Procurement

**What you asked for and what you have.** You asked what changed between ShiftLine's v9.3 ACR and its v9.6 ACR. Five things changed across 56 criteria: one row disappeared, one claim got weaker, two got stronger, and one criterion the vendor previously left unanswered now carries a support claim. Section 4 has the table; § 6 has the counts.

**The one thing to carry into the renewal meeting.** None of this is evidence about the software. Both documents are the vendor's own, neither states how the product was tested or what was sampled, and the city has run no evaluation of v9.6. What moved between June and January is the vendor's wording. A renewal decision that treats "two criteria improved" as a product fact is resting on a sentence, not a measurement.

**If you need to know whether v9.6 actually behaves differently**, that is a scoped verification engagement against the live v9.6 tenant — a WCAG-EM sample, then a claims-delta report that puts each of the vendor's claims next to what we observed. That is the only path from "the document changed" to "the product changed." Your earlier `mar-2026v1` engagement does not substitute: it sampled the v9.3 demo tenant, it is closed, and its findings are not v9.6 evidence.

**Four items to raise with the vendor, in priority order.** All four are cheap asks that cost nothing to make and sharpen the renewal review considerably:

1. **1.4.3 Contrast — why did this change?** The v9.3 report said all text meets 4.5:1; the v9.6 report says body text on the reporting dashboard does not, with the fix deferred to v9.7. Ask directly whether the dashboard changed between releases or whether the earlier blanket claim was wrong. The answer tells you how much the rest of the document is worth. Also ask for a v9.7 date, since the remediation currently points at a version you cannot evaluate.
2. **1.2.2 Captions — why was the row removed?** No explanation is given, and the neighbouring 1.2.3 row still asserts there is no prerecorded media in the product. Either the row should still read `not-applicable` on the same grounds, or 1.2.3 is now wrong. The v9.6 document is one criterion short of the catalog it declares.
3. **3.1.2 Language of Parts — do not read this as a fix.** The v9.3 report used `not-evaluated`, a term the catalog restricts to Level AAA; on a Level AA row it means only that the vendor had not looked. The v9.6 `supports` is the first claim ever made on this criterion, not a defect being cleared. Ask what testing supports it.
4. **Ask both documents' method.** Neither ACR states an evaluation method, a sample set, or a tested configuration, and both leave all four Section 508 chapters — including functional performance criteria and support documentation and services — marked "Not addressed in this report." For a 508 procurement that is a standing gap in both cycles, not something that drifted. Asking the vendor to state its method is the single highest-value request on this list, because every other claim in both documents inherits it.

**What we did not do.** We did not test the product, did not file anything with the vendor, did not produce or amend an ACR, and did not read any of ShiftLine's claims as verified. This report is analysis of two documents, prepared for your decision — the renewal call, and any conformance statement the city makes on the strength of these documents, remain yours.
